item.group_name: Image edits (the user brings a picture)
item.title: Portrait From a Seventies Film

turns.text: Make this look like a still from a 1970s movie—warm faded colours and film grain. Keep her recognisable and keep the square framing. No text.

item.tests: Applies a convincing 1970s film treatment while preserving the uploaded portrait's identity and composition.

answer_sheet.Style and mood: A nostalgic 1970s colour film still, with warm faded colours and visible film grain.
answer_sheet.What to preserve: Her identity, curly dark hair, sweater, pose and park setting.
answer_sheet.Size and format: One square image; free-tier resolution is fine.

must_haves: The woman remains recognisable as the woman in the source portrait.
Her curly dark hair, sweater and head-and-shoulders framing are retained.
The park background remains identifiable rather than becoming a different setting.
Warm, faded colour grading and visible film grain give the image a 1970s film-still appearance.
The output is square and contains no added text.

dialog.agent:
The cheapest listed option for this edit is **Flux 2 Klein: from 5 credits for one 640 × 640 image**, available on the free plan. I haven’t run anything or spent any credits. I can’t verify a firmer total with the tools available here.

I’d preserve her recognisable features and the square composition, adding **warm, faded 1970s film colours, softened contrast and subtle film grain—with no text**.

To keep costs down:
- Generate just **one image at 640 × 640**, the smallest listed size.
- Skip upscaling and extra variations.
- “Shorter” doesn’t apply to a still image.

**Would you like to proceed on that basis, or do you need a confirmed exact price first?**

approvals.name: edit_image

style.prompt: Edit this portrait to look like an authentic still from a 1970s movie. Preserve the woman's identity, recognisable facial features, expression, hairstyle, clothing, pose, and original square framing and park composition. Apply a restrained vintage photochemical film grade: warm faded colours, muted greens, gently warm skin tones, soft contrast, slightly lifted blacks, gentle highlight rolloff, and subtle organic 35mm film grain. Keep realistic natural skin texture and the subject recognisable; do not reshape or beautify her face. No text, titles, captions, logos, watermarks, film borders, or added objects.
